Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 71, titled *Pacchatogamana* ("Walking behind"), is a monastic training rule (*sekhiya*) belonging to the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

The rule forms part of a shared stock of monastic etiquette common to early Buddhist traditions. Within the Pali Canon, direct parallels exist in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (Sk 71), the Bhikkhu Parivāra (Sekhiya 71), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Sk 71), the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha (Sk 71), and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra (Sekhiya 71). Extensive cross-tradition parallels are preserved in the Vinayas of other early Buddhist schools, including Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, Sarvāstivāda, and Mūlasarvāstivāda texts preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan.
